sections.title: What you will learn to say

blocks.text: This lesson is about joining two actions: what you like doing, what you want to do, what you want someone else to do, and why you do something. The second action takes -ing or to — the first word decides which.

examples.en: I enjoy exploring new places.
I intend to stay here.
I want you to read aloud.
I wear a coat to keep warm.

blocks.text: After enjoy, finish, avoid and do not mind, the second action takes -ing: I enjoy exploring new places. Do not put to here.

formula.text: enjoy / finish / avoid / do not mind

examples.en: I enjoy exploring new places.
I must finish writing the summary.
I avoid causing conflict.
examples.translation: I try not to start arguments

examples.en: I do not mind receiving criticism.
I cannot risk losing my job.

fixes.wrong: I enjoy to explore new places.
I do not mind to receive criticism.
fixes.right: I do not mind receiving criticism.

drill.why: After enjoy the second action takes -ing.

blocks.text: After want, need, hope, plan, intend, expect, promise and offer, the second action takes to and stays as in the dictionary: I intend to stay here. After to: no -ing, no -s.

formula.text: want / need / hope / plan / intend / promise

examples.en: I intend to stay here.
I hope to start over.
examples.translation: I would like a new start

examples.en: I plan to travel light.
I promise to keep you posted.
examples.translation: I will tell you the news

examples.en: I do not want to lose touch.
examples.translation: I want us to stay in contact

sections.title: want you to — what you want from someone

blocks.text: To say what you want another person to do: want / need + person + to + action. I want you to read aloud. Not want that you, and not your — use the person: you, him, her.

examples.en: I want you to read aloud.
I need you to straighten the rug.
I want you to tell the truth.
I need you to pay attention.
I want you to wait your turn.

fixes.wrong: I want that you read aloud.
fixes.right: I want you to read aloud.

fixes.wrong: I want your to approve the plan.
fixes.right: I want you to approve the plan.

fixes.wrong: I want you approve the plan.
fixes.right: I want you to approve the plan.

drill.prompt: Say that you want the other person to read aloud.

blocks.text: To say why you do something, just use to + action: I wear a coat to keep warm. Do not use for here: for learn is a mistake.

formula.text: why: action as in the dictionary

examples.en: I wear a coat to keep warm.
I join a study group to learn English.
examples.translation: that is the reason I join

examples.en: I leave early to beat the traffic.
I compare prices to save money.
I take notes to remember the ideas.

fixes.wrong: I join a study group for learn English.
fixes.right: I join a study group to learn English.

fixes.wrong: I join a study group to learning English.
fixes.right: I join a study group to learn English.

drill.question: It is cold outside. Explain why you wear a coat.
drill.optionA: I wear a coat for keep warm.
drill.optionB: I wear a coat to keep warm.
drill.explain: The reason is to + action; for does not work here.

fixes.wrong: I enjoy to explore new places.
I want that you read aloud.
fixes.right: I want you to read aloud.

fixes.wrong: I join a study group for learn English.
fixes.right: I join a study group to learn English.

fixes.wrong: The no smoking sign means you mustn't to smoke.
fixes.right: The no smoking sign means you mustn't smoke.

blocks.text: -ing or to? The first word decides. enjoy, finish, avoid, mind — -ing. want, need, hope, plan, promise — to. Learn them in pairs: enjoy exploring, want to stay.
Enjoy, finish, avoid — + -ing. Want, hope, plan — + to. What you want from someone — want you to. The reason — to. After to, always the action as in the dictionary.

examples.en: I enjoy making friends.
I need to check the timetable.
I want to make you laugh.
examples.translation: I want you to be happy
